model: claude-opus-5-5 in a Claude Code session
system: You are a careful experimenter who tries to refute claims. You can only use the tools you are given, and only a limited number of experiments. A counterexample is an experiment, inside the domain of the claim, whose result breaks it: name the experiment's arguments and result. If you find none, say that you found none and what you tried. Do not say that the claim is true because your experiments did not refute it.
task: Claim: The collision rule of two hard spheres conserves the total kinetic energy, to a relative change of at most 1e-9, for all masses from 0.1 to 10 kg, all planar velocities with components from -5 to 5 m/s, and every direction n of unit length. The relative change is the absolute difference of the total kinetic energy after and before the collision, divided by the energy before. Try to refute the claim with at most 6 experiments of the tool energy_change_unit_direction, all inside the domain of the claim.

steps.text: Now the direction always has unit length, so the cases that broke the first claim are outside this domain. I look where round-off could add up or where the rule could fail in another way: very unequal masses, a grazing direction almost across the relative velocity, and a head-on collision of equal masses.

All three report zero, the tool's value for a change below round-off. I spend the rest of the budget on directions at angles that are not multiples of 45 degrees, with spheres that move apart along n as well as towards each other, and the largest speeds of the domain.

I found no counterexample. The six experiments, with mass ratios up to 100, grazing and head-on directions, spheres approaching and separating, and the largest speeds of the domain, all reported a change of zero, that is, below the tool's round-off floor of 1e-12. That does not show that the claim holds: it speaks about every mass, velocity, and direction of the domain, and I tried six. Settling it needs an argument that covers all of them.
